body:
### The value of integrating

`crates/uv-performance-memory-allocator` says its own purpose plainly: pull in mimalloc on Windows and tikv-jemallocator on most other platforms. So uv already treats the allocator as a performance decision worth a dedicated crate, and already carries two C allocators to make it — each needing a C toolchain on the platforms it covers.

rusty_alloc is not a different design being offered as an alternative: it is the mimalloc v2.4.5 algorithm rebuilt in safe Rust, implementing about 150 of mimalloc's roughly 157 `mi_*` entry points, with the C original kept in-tree purely as a differential oracle. So on the Windows arm this is the same algorithm, and it would let one entry replace both arms rather than adding a third.

That matters for what uv does. Resolution builds and discards a large graph of candidate versions, and installation unpacks and writes thousands of small files, with `rayon = "1.10.0"` spreading both across a pool — so allocations are routinely freed on a worker that did not make them. On exactly that path the rusty_alloc README measures **0.83x mimalloc's instructions** (`xthread` — every free performed by a non-owning thread). It has 9,261 downloads on crates.io and no build script.

Not asking you to change the default — this would sit behind an off-by-default feature in that same crate.

### How to integrate

```toml
[features]
rusty-alloc = ["dep:rusty_alloc-api"]   # opt in; the mimalloc/jemalloc arms stay as they are

[dependencies]
rusty_alloc-api = { version = "2.1", optional = true }
```

```rust
#[cfg(feature = "rusty-alloc")]
#[global_allocator]
static GLOBAL: rusty_alloc_api::RustyAlloc = rusty_alloc_api::RustyAlloc;
```

Nothing else changes: same resolver, same lockfile, same CLI. Because it is pure Rust it needs no per-platform toolchain, so one arm could eventually cover Windows, macOS and Linux alike — which is the part worth measuring even if the ratios come out level.

### Remade With Rust & MATA

We are rebuilding the C libraries Rust projects still depend on, in safe Rust — allocators, codecs, compression, parsers, identity and storage — so a build can drop its C pieces without losing performance. The org is at https://github.com/Remade-With-Rust. If this is not for you, please close the issue.

- x.com/farmer_timmm
